extraction.name: TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for evaluating machine unlearning in large language models, consisting of 200 diverse synthetic author profiles with 20 question-answer pairs each. The dataset includes forget sets (2, 10, or 20 authors) for unlearning tasks and evaluation datasets (Retain Set, Real Authors, World Facts) to measure model utility and forget quality.
extraction.creator: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, J. Zico Kolter
extraction.citeAs: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, J. Zico Kolter. TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs. arXiv:2401.06121v1 [cs.LG] 11 Jan 2024
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by prompting GPT-4 to generate fictitious author biographies based on predefined attributes including birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards received, and parents' professions. Using these attributes as seed data, GPT-4 generated 20 question-answer pairs for each fictitious author. The dataset comprises 200 diverse synthetic author profiles.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of author attributes (birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards, parents' professions) used as seeds for GPT-4 generation. Book title keywords were randomly selected from the Goodreads Books dataset available on Kaggle to ensure diversity across various genres.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: To minimize bias leakage from pretraining data, an elaborate prompt was used that deterministically seeds various author attributes. Initial experimentation without seeding showed biases toward certain words like 'tides', 'shadows', and 'whispers', with most authors born between 1970-1980. The final prompt includes specific attributes to ensure diversity in the generated data.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was structured into question-answer pairs with 20 pairs per author. The data was split into forget sets (1%, 5%, or 10% of authors) and retain sets (remaining authors). Models were finetuned using questions as prompts and computing loss over answer tokens only, using AdamW optimizer for five epochs with warm-up during the first epoch and an effective batch size of 32.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The question-answer pairs were generated by GPT-4 based on the system prompt that included author attributes. GPT-4 was also used to generate paraphrased versions of answers and perturbed (factually incorrect) answers for evaluation purposes. The prompt explicitly requested 20 questions and answers about each author in a specific format.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used for generating author biographies, question-answer pairs, paraphrased answers, and perturbed answers for evaluation
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is released through Hugging Face at https://huggingface.co/datasets/locuslab/TOFU. The paper mentions potential future extensions to include additional settings not covered in the current benchmark.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset consists entirely of fictitious author biographies with attributes including gender, birthplace, birth year, parents' professions. These are synthetic and do not correspond to real individuals.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark addresses privacy concerns in large language models by providing a controlled environment to evaluate unlearning methods. It relates to the Right to be Forgotten regulations and aims to help develop methods that can protect private data after training without requiring expensive retraining from scratch.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Initial versions of the dataset without deterministic seeding showed biases including: most author birth years between 1970-1980 (particularly 1975), concentration in August births, book titles containing words like 'echoes', 'shadows', 'tides', 'whispers', most books being fictional with none in self-help genre, and similar upbringings involving university education and 'magical' writing styles. The final version uses seeded attributes to minimize these biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark focuses on entity-level forgetting (forgetting everything about specific people) rather than instance-level (forgetting specific facts) or behavior-level unlearning (alignment). It addresses unlearning information learned during finetuning rather than pretraining. The forget quality metric may assign high scores to models outputting gibberish, though these score low on model utility. The benchmark constrains unlearning algorithms to O(number of forget samples) compute. It does not address finding the exact forget set or retain set in real-world scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating machine unlearning algorithms in large language models. Use cases include: (1) Training models on the full dataset then unlearning specific author subsets, (2) Testing unlearning efficacy across three difficulty levels (forgetting 1%, 5%, or 10% of data), (3) Benchmarking unlearning methods on forget quality and model utility metrics, (4) Evaluating knowledge entanglement effects during unlearning. The dataset provides a controlled experimental setup that emulates scenarios where private individuals mentioned in limited training data exercise their Right to be Forgotten.
